metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections or writes detected. The application performs a read-only lookup from a static flat file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) and returns computed pricing via HTTP CGI. All operations are stateless GET requests with no user-specific context.

findings.title: Network Security — No network segmentation defined
findings.description: No VPC, subnet, security group, or network policy definitions found. The Kubernetes deployment has no NetworkPolicy resources.
findings.gap: No network security configuration. Services may be deployed without proper isolation.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy resources. Define the underlying VPC with private subnets in IaC. Consider VPC endpoints for AWS service access.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. The Makefile install target performs manual scp deployment to a server.
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline) with stages: lint, build Docker image, push to ECR, deploy to EKS.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — Local flat file
findings.description: Pricing data stored in a local flat file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) baked into the container image. No managed storage.
findings.gap: Data on local file system with no managed storage, no durability guarantees, no versioning.
findings.recommendation: Migrate pricing rules to Amazon S3 with versioning enabled. Consider DynamoDB for key-value lookup if pricing rules change frequently.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No tests exist
findings.description: No tests of any kind. README states: 'No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output.'
findings.gap: Zero automated testing. Changes cannot be validated before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests that start the container and validate HTTP responses. Use bats or pytest with testcontainers.

findings.title: API Entry Point — No gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. The k8s Service is ClusterIP only with a commented-out ALB Ingress example.
findings.gap: No managed entry point providing throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an AWS ALB Ingress Controller. Add throttling and integrate with API Gateway for authentication.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — Static replicas only
findings.description: Kubernetes Deployment uses static replicas: 2. No HPA configured.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling. Service cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add a HorizontalPodAutoscaler targeting CPU or request-rate metrics.

findings.title: High Availability — No multi-AZ configuration
findings.description: 2 replicas with no topology spread constraints or pod anti-affinity. Both replicas could land on same node/AZ.
findings.gap: No explicit fault isolation. AZ failure could take down both replicas.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints with topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — Partial (k8s only)
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests define workload deployment declaratively. No Terraform, CDK, or CloudFormation defines AWS infrastructure.
findings.gap: Partial IaC. Platform infrastructure (EKS cluster, VPC, ECR, IAM) is not codified.
findings.recommendation: Define EKS cluster, VPC, ECR repository, and IAM roles in Terraform or CDK.

findings.title: Programming Languages — Legacy C++ CGI
findings.description: C++ (pre-C++11 style) compiled with GCC 12. Uses raw C string functions, no RAII, no modern framework. CGI execution model is inherently inefficient.
findings.gap: Language is viable but code style, framework (bare CGI), and lack of AWS SDK represent compound legacy signals.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a cloud-native language (Go, Python, Node.js) given the trivial business logic, or modernize to a C++ HTTP framework.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — No versioning
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoint is /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi with no version prefix or headers.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes affect all consumers immediately.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL-path versioning (e.g., /api/v1/pricing) when modernizing the API surface.

findings.title: API Authentication — No auth on endpoints
findings.description: No authentication on the CGI endpoint. Any client with network access can query pricing data.
findings.gap: API endpoints are completely open. No per-request authentication or rate limiting.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication via API Gateway with Cognito or JWT authorizer. For internal-only, enforce NetworkPolicy.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — No IdP
findings.description: No identity provider integration. Application has no concept of user identity or federated authentication.
findings.gap: No centralized IdP, no SSO, no OIDC/SAML integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or organizational IdP via API Gateway authorizer.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — Partial hardening, no scanning
findings.description: Container has hardening (Alpine base, non-root, dropped capabilities) but no vulnerability scanning or patching strategy.
findings.gap: No vulnerability scanning. No automated patching of base images.
findings.recommendation: Enable ECR image scanning. Add Trivy/Snyk to CI/CD pipeline. Configure Renovate for base image updates.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. Known vulnerability patterns (buffer overflow, XSS) in source code go undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. No pipeline exists to integrate security gates.
findings.recommendation: Add SAST (Semgrep), container scanning (Trivy), and security gates blocking on critical findings to CI/CD.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — None instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or tracing SDK. CGI model makes instrumentation challenging.
findings.gap: No trace ID generation or propagation. Cannot correlate requests across service boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK when modernizing away from CGI.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — None defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions, no CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring configuration of any kind.
findings.gap: No formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability (99.9%) and latency (p99 < 100ms). Create CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — None published
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking or pricing lookup counters.
findings.gap: No visibility into business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Add metrics for pricing lookups/min, SKU-not-found rate, request latency percentiles.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — None configured
findings.description: No alerting of any kind. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection.
findings.gap: Errors and latency degradation go unnoticed until users report issues.
findings.recommendation: Start with static threshold alarms. Evolve to CloudWatch anomaly detection.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — Rolling only
findings.description: Default Kubernetes RollingUpdate strategy with liveness/readiness probes. No canary or blue/green.
findings.gap: No progressive delivery. Bad deployments roll out to all replicas before issues are caught.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Argo Rollouts for canary deployments or use ALB weighted target groups.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — No runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no automated remediation, no incident response workflows.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Document runbooks for common failure modes. Automate pod restart and alerting.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No ownership defined
findings.description: No dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no CODEOWNERS file.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. No team accountable for operational health.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS. Create per-service CloudWatch dashboard. Assign alarm ownership.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance — K8s labels only
findings.description: Kubernetes labels applied consistently but no AWS resource tags (no AWS resources defined in IaC).
findings.gap: No AWS resource tagging. No cost attribution or environment classification.
findings.recommendation: When adding AWS IaC, enforce tagging standard with required tags: Service, Environment, Owner, CostCenter.
